consent.title: Connect {app} to Polaris
consent.unverified: The name is what the app says about itself. Check the address it sends you back to.
consent.loopback: This app runs on this computer. Only continue if you just started the connection yourself.
consent.scopesHint: Untick anything it should not do. It can never do more than your account can.
consent.withheld: Asked for, but your account cannot: {scopes}
consent.noneHeld: Your account has none of the permissions this app asks for, so there is nothing to grant.
consent.pickOne: Choose at least one permission, or deny.
consent.later: You can disconnect it at any time under Account > API keys.

errors.client: This link does not name an app Polaris can identify. Start the connection again from the app.
errors.redirect: This link would send you to an address the app never registered, so it was stopped. Start the connection again from the app.
errors.viewingAs: You are viewing Polaris as someone else. Stop viewing as them to connect an app to your own account.
errors.tooMany: Too many connection attempts. Wait a few minutes and start again from the app.
errors.failed: Polaris could not finish connecting the app. Start again from the app.

scopes.chat_use: Read and post in your conversations

connectedApps.title: Connected assistants
connectedApps.intro: Assistants and editors you allowed to act for you over MCP. Each one can do only what you approved, and never more than your account.
connectedApps.empty: No apps connected. Connect one from Account > Downloads.
connectedApps.disconnectDescription: It stops working at once. To use it again, connect it from the app.
connectedApps.failed: That app could not be disconnected. Reload and try again.

assistants.title: AI assistants (MCP)
assistants.intro: Let Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and other assistants work with your Polaris. They sign in here, you choose what each one may do, and you can disconnect them under Account > API keys.

claudeCode.name: Claude Code
claudeCode.step2: In Claude Code, run {command} and choose polaris to sign in.

claude.name: Claude (web and desktop)
claude.step1: Open Customize > Connectors and choose Add custom connector.
claude.step2: Name it Polaris, paste the server URL and choose Add.
claude.step3: Choose Connect and sign in here.
claude.teams: On Team and Enterprise plans, an owner adds it under Organization settings > Connectors first.

chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.step1: Open Settings > Security and login and turn on Developer mode.
chatgpt.step2: Open Plugins, select Add, then Create MCP App.
chatgpt.step3: Name it Polaris. Under Connection, keep Server URL and paste the server URL.
chatgpt.step4: Set Authentication to OAuth. No client ID or secret is needed.
chatgpt.step5: Check I understand and want to continue, then select Create.
chatgpt.step6: Sign in here when ChatGPT asks.
chatgpt.missing: If Add only offers Create plugin and Upload plugin, Developer mode is off. Those two are for packaged plugins, not for a server URL.
chatgpt.plans: Needs a Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Education plan, on the web. In a Business, Enterprise or Education workspace, an admin may have to allow Developer mode first.

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.signIn: Cursor asks you to sign in here the first time it uses Polaris.

vscode.signIn: VS Code asks you to sign in here the first time it uses Polaris.
